incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), S.B.C. 2002, c. 57, ss. 10, 11, 21, 51, and Part 2.1; Business Corporations Act General Regulation, ss. 2–5.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registry, Corporate and House Registries, Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia (Corporate Online portal)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Application (Form 1) and Notice of Articles (Form 2)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an unlimited liability company under the BCA; consideration for shares is determined by the directors or by written shareholder agreement. No escrow account is required by the Registrar for ordinary formation; any subscription funds held by a lawyer must be maintained in a trust account under the Law Society of British Columbia rules.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT: (1) The subscription and issuance of 1,000 ordinary shares at USD 1.00 each, for a total subscription price of USD 1,000, to [Subscriber Name], is approved and accepted. (2) The registered and records office of the company is established at 1111 West Georgia Street, Vancouver, British Columbia, V6E 4M3, Canada. (3) [Director Name] is appointed President; [Director Name] is appointed Secretary; [Director Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until the next annual meeting. (4) The officers are authorized to open corporate bank accounts and execute banking forms. (5) Management shall file all documents necessary to comply with British Columbia laws.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry — Corporate Online (Name Reservation module)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request via the Corporate Online portal. Enter three proposed corporate names in order of preference, including a legal element such as 'Unlimited Liability Corporation' or 'ULC'. Pay the name reservation fee. Await electronic approval of a name reservation number, which is valid for 56 calendar days.
required_dossiers: Corporate name search report (NUANS or BC Registry search)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed name is refused, file a revised name reservation with an alternate name within 14 days. No refund of the name search fee is granted; a written explanation may be requested from the Registrar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constituent Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and legal counsel (BC notary or lawyer); filing prepared for submission to BC Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Notice of Articles, Articles, Incorporation Agreement, and written consent to act of each initial director. For a ULC, the Notice of Articles must state that the company is an unlimited liability company and that shareholders have unlimited liability. Ensure all signature dates are coordinated so that no consent predates the incorporation application.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the filing package is deficient, the Registrar will issue an 'incomplete filing' notice listing defects. Correct and refile the package within 30 days of the notice to preserve the original priority date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Issuance of Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry — Corporate Online (online filing window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed Notice of Articles and Incorporation Application through Corporate Online. Pay the statutory filing fee by credit card or authorized debit. The Registry will review the application and, if compliant, issue the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and a Notice of Filings. Download and retain the certificate for subsequent business registrations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues a query or refusal, respond with corrected information within 14 calendar days. If no response is made, the application is deemed withdrawn and the filing fee may be forfeited. A fresh application may be filed after correcting the issue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inaugural Board Meeting and Adoption of First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Initial directors of the company (internal corporate governance; minutes maintained at registered office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon receipt of the Certificate of Incorporation, convene an inaugural board meeting. The directors must adopt the first board resolution covering share issuance, registered office adoption, and officer appointments. Where any director is absent, execute a written resolution in lieu of a meeting under section 66 of the BCA. The minutes and director consents must be placed in the corporate records book kept at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a named officer refuses to act, the board may appoint a substitute officer by ordinary resolution and file a director/officer change notice with the Registry within 15 days. Any defect in the resolution is cured by subsequent unanimous board consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxation Registrations and Municipal / Physical Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (Business Number); BC Ministry of Finance (Provincial Sales Tax); City of Vancouver Business Licence Office (or applicable municipality)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for a federal Business Number through the CRA's New Business Registration portal and elect to open a GST/HST account if required. Register for BC PST under the Provincial Sales Tax Act using the BC Corporate Online portal. If a physical warehouse or office is established, obtain a municipal business licence and comply with local zoning and building permits. For any warehousing operation, register with BC Workers' Compensation Board (WorkSafeBC) for occupational health and safety coverage.
required_dossiers: Notice of registered office and first address
Lease or ownership document for the property
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or BC Ministry of Finance sends a query, provide the requested documentation within 30 days. For a municipal business licence, cure any nonconformity by submitting updated building or zoning records within 10 business days. WorkSafeBC clearance can be expedited through the online registration portal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the undertaking is an online retail and logistics operation, not an industrial activity requiring a specific provincial operating licence.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required under British Columbia law; only a municipal business licence and CRA/WorkSafeBC registrations are mandatory for the described commercial activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: British Columbia Ministry of Environment and Climate Change Strategy
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — retail distribution and warehousing are not assessable activities under the Environmental Assessment Act; no environmental assessment registration is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If a warehouse or fulfilment centre is operated, comply with the BC Municipal Wastewater Regulation for any indirect industrial or non-domestic discharge; comply with the Canadian Environmental Protection Act for residual combustion emissions from heating equipment; maintain waste handling in accordance with the BC Recycling Regulation if packaging waste exceeds 200 kg/month.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a building occupancy permit from the local municipality for any leased premises; secure a fire safety clearance under the BC Fire Code for warehouse storage; register with WorkSafeBC for occupational health and safety coverage; perform a structural load inspection if racking systems are installed in the fulfilment warehouse.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) exercises anti-money-laundering oversight; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) prudenitally regulates Canadian banks and clearing operations
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account and capital-account convertibility with no general foreign-exchange control statute. The Currency Act makes the Canadian dollar legal tender, but residents and non-residents may freely hold, use, and transfer foreign currency. Inbound equity injections, shareholder loans, and outbound profit remittances are not subject to Central Bank approval. Profit remittances from a BC Unlimited Liability Corporation (ULC) to non-resident shareholders are subject to Part XIII withholding tax on dividends (statutory 25%, treaty-reduced under the Canada-United States Tax Convention and third-country treaties). The principal compliance hurdles are Canadian banking AML/KYC onboarding, FINTRAC large-transaction reporting (CAD 10,000 threshold), and documentary proof of source of funds and ultimate beneficial ownership. Capital distributions and returns of paid-up capital may be remitted without withholding if properly documented as return of capital rather than dividend; CRA forms NR4, NR301, and NR302 are required as applicable.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory surrender, repatriation, or forced conversion requirement for export proceeds. There is no mandatory timeline for conversion into Canadian dollars and no prescribed conversion ratio. An exporting ULC may retain 100% of foreign-currency proceeds in domestic or offshore accounts. Canadian banks are, however, required to report any transaction involving CAD 10,000 or more to FINTRAC, and cross-border electronic funds transfers are subject to reportable-transaction monitoring. No Bank of Canada declaration or export-license is required for furniture e-commerce sales.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account (CAD, USD, and foreign-currency sub-accounts)
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account with cross-border US Dollar cash management and wire clearing
Operational Account with import trade finance and commercial letter-of-credit facility
Operational Account and foreign-exchange hedging counterparty account
Operational Account with SWIFT MT103/MT202 payment rails and access to Lynx clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium supplemental viability. Offshore digital EMI products (e.g., Wise Business, Payoneer, and similar specialized FX platforms) may be used for low-value disbursements and cross-border vendor payments but are not a substitute for a regulated Canadian bank account. The primary legal constraint is that an offshore EMI is not a member of Payments Canada and therefore cannot directly settle through Lynx or the Canadian Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS). In practice, an EMI must operate through a Canadian sponsor bank, creating settlement risk and an additional intermediary. EMI accounts are not CDIC-insured, and the ULC remains fully liable under its unlimited-liability structure for any outstanding obligations. The feasibility rating is 'Low' for capital escrow and treasury concentration and 'Medium' for small invoice disbursements, supplier trial runs, and sub-CAD 10,000 operational FX payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Canadian federal banking law does not mandate physical presence as a universal statutory KYC rule, but Tier-1 Canadian commercial banks commonly require at least one authorized director, officer, or signatory to attend an in-branch identity-verification interview at a designated commercial banking centre, typically in Vancouver or Toronto. Remote video/electronic KYC is available only where the bank's client-acceptance policy permits non-face-to-face verification and where all ultimate beneficial owners are resident in a FATF-equivalent jurisdiction. For a BC-registered ULC with non-resident shareholders and unlimited shareholder liability, the practical onboarding reality is that a physical interview for the primary signing officer is highly likely. Professional-director or nominee-director arrangements will not waive the UBO identification requirement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unlimited liability structure combined with non-resident shareholders and a pass-through tax classification election
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the Certificate of Unlimited Liability Corporation from BC Corporate Registry, the Notice of Articles, the unanimous shareholder agreement, the CRA letter confirming business number and GST/HST account, audited or reviewed financial statements, notarized corporate resolutions authorizing account opening, updated register of directors and register of shareholders, and a legal opinion from a BC solicitor confirming the ULC's validity, limited-purpose use, and unlimited-liability exposure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce revenue model relying on Stripe and Affirm BNPL settlement aggregation, which may present unverifiable B2C transaction flows and refund/chargeback complexity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the executed Stripe merchant agreement and Affirm BNPL integration agreement, merchant account identifiers, 90-day settlement history export, transaction-level reporting, refund and chargeback policy, PCI DSS attestation of compliance, and a reconciliation model demonstrating that platform settlements map to identifiable customer orders and warehouse fulfilment records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registered office (law firm) versus operational presence at an oversized-furniture fulfilment warehouse, triggering address-consistency red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the BC municipal business licence, warehouse lease agreement, property utility invoices, commercial general liability insurance certificate, employer or payroll evidence if staff exist in BC, and a signed director attestation confirming that the registered office is retained solely for service-of-process and statutory correspondence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdictions in the offshore supply chain for imported oversized furniture (e.g., PRC, Vietnam, or other Asian manufacturing sources)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Assemble supplier due-diligence files, valid commercial invoices and bills of lading, HS-code customs entry summaries, purchase order contracts, quality-inspection certificates, freight-forwarder credentials, and banking references documentating prior settlement history, together with a complete country-by-country exposure statement for the ultimate beneficial ownership.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections from non-resident shareholders must be routed by SWIFT MT103 single-customer credit transfer using the beneficiary bank's SWIFT/BIC, the ULC's Canadian transit number and account number, and a clear Field 70 remittance narrative stating 'Shareholder capital contribution to BC ULC' or 'Subordinated shareholder loan'. No Canadian exchange-control approval is required, but the receiving bank will require a source-of-funds declaration and may perform a FINTRAC large-transaction report if the amount equals or exceeds CAD 10,000. Documentation should include a shareholder resolution authorizing the contribution, a subscription agreement or loan agreement, and CRA-filed or notional paid-up-capital records. Inbound funds should first land in a dedicated Capital Escrow Account or segregated operational clearing account, never commingled with e-commerce payments from Stripe of Affirm, and the bank may require a quarantine period pending KYC verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier and freight settlements must be executed through cleared corporate banking rails. Direct supplier payments should use SWIFT MT103 with full beneficiary details and HS-code / commercial-invoice references in Field 70. CAD-denominated settlement is cleared through Payments Canada's Lynx real-time gross settlement system in excess of the ACSS threshold, while USD-denominated balances may be cleared via U.S. Fedwire or Clearing House Interbank Payments System (CHIPS) through the Canadian bank's correspondent network. For higher-value or repeat furniture imports, a Commercial Letter of Credit issued by the Canadian bank pursuant to ICC UCP600 provides documentary risk mitigation; for oversized-freight logistics, standby letters of credit or bank-guarantee instruments may secure obligations to freight forwarders. The treasury policy should mandate dual-approval for all outbound wires and the retention of all MT103 confirmation records for CRA and FINTRAC audit purposes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Canadian-dollar / U.S.-dollar FX forwards on maturities up to 12 months to hedge receivables and supplier costs
Deliverable Canadian-dollar / Euro FX forwards for European furniture-decor sourcing
Deliverable Canadian-dollar / Offshore Renminbi (CNH) forwards for China-based supplier payments
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted or illiquid emerging-market currencies where physical delivery is not feasible
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CAD vs USD) to align debt-service obligations with revenue denominated in U.S. dollars
FX swaps (rollovers) to manage temporary liquidity mismatches without creating a net speculative position

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report (Business Corporations Act, s. 274)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: BC Registrar of Companies, Ministry of Finance, British Columbia (Corporate Online / BC Registries)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 calendar months (60 days) following each anniversary of the date of incorporation; filed via BC Registries' online filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing places the ULC in arrears; two consecutive unfiled annual reports permit the Registrar to administratively dissolve the company (strike-off); restoration after dissolution requires filing all overdue reports and a CAD 500 reinstatement fee plus late-filing surcharges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporate Income Tax Return (including federal and provincial schedules; disclosure schedules if Article IV(7) ULC pass-through election is claimed)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after the fiscal year-end (e.g., June 30 for a calendar-year-end ULC); the return must be filed electronically for fiscal years ending after 2020
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty equal to 5% of any unpaid tax balance plus 1% per complete month of delay (capped at 12 months); interest is charged on late instalments and balances; a nil-balance ULC normally incurs no monetary penalty, but chronic non-filing triggers CRA compliance action, asset garnishment, and director liability for withheld amounts.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday; Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) eligibility reduces the combined rate to 11% on the first C$500,000 of active business income via the federal small business deduction (9%) and BC small business deduction (2%). Other incentives: 30% CCA accelerated rates for equipment, SR&ED investment tax credits, and BC local tax credits (not furniture retail).

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed electronically via Canada Revenue Agency My Business Access or a CRA-approved NETFILE/T2 service provider
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly income tax instalments due when prior-year or current-year tax payable exceeds C$3,000
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Six months after the taxation year-end (ITA s.150(2)). A BC ULC with a December 31 year-end files by June 30; with a March 31 year-end, by September 30.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business number (BN), legal name, registered office address, and jurisdiction of incorporation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: File under the ULC's Canadian BN and legal name. Do not use the non-resident shareholder's foreign tax identifier; the ULC is a separate Canadian taxpayer.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxation year opening and closing dates (YYYY-MM-DD)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the fiscal year specified in the ULC's articles. A mismatch with the foreign parent's tax year is permissible but can complicate consolidated reporting and PDTA credit computations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income (loss) per IFRS/US GAAP financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide income if the ULC is a Canadian-resident corporation. Non-resident shareholders may not allocate US income to the ULC to offset Canadian losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments, loss carryovers (20-year non-capital, 3-year back, indefinite capital loss carryforward) and tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim deductions that are Canadian-law compliant. Losses of the foreign parent cannot be used to reduce the ULC's Canadian taxable income; only the ULC's own loss carryovers are deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Part I federal taxable income tax at 15%, then Line 65 federal abatement and provincial allocation to BC at 12%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the BC provincial allocation schedule using the ULC's actual and qualified Canadian labour and gross revenues. For a remote-service e-commerce seller, the allocation may reflect only BC-location factors if all selling effort is located outside Canada.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty equal to 5% of unpaid tax at the deadline plus 1% per full month late until a maximum of 12 months (ITA s.162). Interest accrues on unpaid amounts at the CRA prescribed rate. Repeated failure to file may trigger an additional penalty of up to 10% of the tax payable.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% (Part XIII non-resident withholding tax on dividends paid from a Canadian-resident ULC). Reduced to 5% under the Canada–US Income Tax Convention if the beneficial owner is a US corporation controlling at least 10% of the voting power; otherwise 15% for portfolio dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before dividend payment, the non-resident shareholder must present to the ULC a completed Form NR301 (Declaration of Beneficial Owner) and a valid IRS Form 6166 (Certificate of Residence) issued by the United States. The ULC as withholding agent must retain the documents and file an annual Part XIII return and remittance summary with the CRA. Refund claims under s.227(6) require filing Form NR7-D within two years of the end of the calendar year in which the excess was withheld.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rates: interest 25%, royalties 25%. Under Canada–US DTA: arm's-length interest paid to a US resident is generally exempt from Canadian withholding tax (0%); royalties for industrial/commercial/scientific equipment or patent rights are subject to 10%, while copyright royalties for literary, artistic, and scientific works (including software) are subject to 0%. The NR301/Form 6166 protocol applies to all treaty-reduced rates.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation (Local File and Master File) is administratively required when the aggregate fair market value of controlled transactions with non-residents exceeds C$1 million in a fiscal year. For multinational groups with consolidated turnover greater than C$10 million, CRA generally expects a Master File. Transactions below C$1 million may rely on simplified documentation (contemporaneous invoices, pricing policy, and a written arm's-length justification).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not have standalone Economic Substance Regulations; however, CRA invokes the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s.245 ITA) and substance-over-form doctrine to counter shell conduits. A BC ULC with no employees, no physical inventory storage in Canada, and no logistical decision-making is exposed to re-characterization and denial of treaty benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting online-sales revenue; issuing fictitious invoices for oversized-furniture freight expenses; or concealing Stripe/Affirm settlement funds in an off-shore account without declaring Canadian profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under ITA s.239(1) carries a penalty of up to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded plus imprisonment for up to 5 years. Civil gross-negligence penalty under s.163.2 is 50% of the understated tax (minimum C$100). Interest and CRA enforcement costs apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false T2 returns or cause withholding-tax evasion are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax shortfall and penalties; they may be criminally prosecuted, banned from board service, and in serious cases issued travel injunctions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the ULC as a bare conduit with no physical location, personnel, inventory, or real commercial function, used exclusively to route cross-border furniture sales to a US parent for treaty-shopping benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may apply GAAR to disregard the ULC; reassess the parent as the true taxpayer; impose interest and gross-negligence penalties; and deny treaty withholding reductions. The BC Registry may strike off a non-active company for failing to file annual returns or provide its corporate dossier.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors involved in orchestrating a sham may be personally assessed under ITA s.227.1 for unremitted Part XIII withholding tax if they controlled the entity and failed to act with reasonable care.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling oversized furniture to a related US distribution entity at no profit or below cost, or paying excessive intercompany logistics fees to an offshore sister company, eroding Canadian taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA adjusts the price to an arm's-length amount under s.247(2); the net adjustment is subject to full tax plus interest. A separate s.247(3) penalty of 10% of the net adjustment applies if the adjustment exceeds either C$5 million or 10% of gross revenue and the taxpayer failed to make reasonable efforts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable for transfer-pricing penalties, but if they approved contrived transactions with the intent to evade, they may be jointly and severally liable under the Tax Evasion rules and subject to oppression or fraud claims.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file the BC Annual Report or maintain the register of ‘individuals with significant control’; or neglecting to implement a FINTRAC compliance program when the ULC receives large cash settlements or has a blend of cross-border cryptocurrency/fiat payment rails.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: BC Business Corporations Act: late annual-report fees and eventual dissolution after two years. Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act: administrative monetary penalties (up to C$1 million) for non-registration or reporting failures; obstruction or false reporting may lead to imprisonment up to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for late annual-report fees and penalty amounts imposed under BC law. For money-laundering activities directed or authorized by directors, personal criminal liability attaches under the PCMLTFA and Criminal Code, which may include imprisonment and order of restitution to the Crown.
